articles.title: Tourette syndrome campaigner John Davidson to watch Bafta Scotland awards in separate ‘relaxed’ space
articles.summary: Decision follows independent review into handling of February ceremony, where his involuntary tics caused a BBC crisis. John Davidson, the Tourette syndrome campaigner whose outburst at the British Academy film awards in February led to a crisis for Bafta (British Academy of Film and Television…
body: In a letter sent to Bafta members on Thursday, the organisation’s chair Sara Putt and CEO Jane Millichip said that, after an independent review, Bafta had “strengthened and centralised our safeguarding, risk assessment and compliance processes” and had made arrangements in consultation with “safeguarding and inclusion experts” for Davidson’s attendance at the awards ceremony organised by Bafta’s Scottish branch, which is due to take place in November.

For the Bafta Scotland awards ceremony, Bafta says that, in accordance with Davidson’s own suggestion, he will “watch the ceremony via video link from a separate relaxed space within the venue with his family and friends”.

I Swear, the film based on Davidson’s life, is the leading contender with seven nominations at the Bafta Scotland awards, including all three nominations in the best film actor category, for Peter Mullan, Robert Aramayo and Scott Ellis Watson, and best film actress for Shirley Henderson. Aramayo unexpectedly won best actor at the national Bafta film awards in February.

articles.title: ‘These early friendships are huge romances’: Extra Geography’s lessons in teenage love
articles.summary: Rose Tremain, along with the cast and crew of a new film updating her 1950s story to the early 00s, remember the intensity of these relationships and explain why its story has not dated. A few years ago, Rose Tremain was asked to name her biggest disappointment. Her reply?
body: “I’ve been delighted by this whole project,” she says, still sounding surprised. Tremain adores the script, adapted from her elegant five-page story by playwright and Succession scriptwriter Miriam Battye. At their first meeting, Battye told her it would easily transfer to the modern day: “I felt really pleased about that,” says Tremain. “It’s not just a little relic from my past. It has relevance now.”

She is equally delighted with the finished film: “To make a 90-minute movie, Miriam had to do a lot of inventing. And I think all the inventing that she’s done is very, very right for the story. She completely understood it and yet made it her own, which, honestly …” Tremain pauses. “In cinema, I don’t know how often that happens. Usually when somebody says they’re going to write your thing, they take it in a direction which you can’t recognise at all.”

articles.title: Derek vs Derek review – farmers go head to head in rewilding rivalry with real bite
articles.summary: Two Devon neighbours face off over the future of the countryside in this warm, wry documentary about farming, conservation and some troublesome wild boar. This ebulliently accessible but never tacky British documentary finds a delightfully sneaky way to explore debates around environmental damage…
body: The twosome at the heart of the story are neighbours Derek Gow and Derek Banbury, two men in late middle age in wellies with bellies whose roughly equal-sized allotments of land (about 120 hectares) abut each other in Devon, near Dartmoor. Twinkly eyed, West Country-accented Banbury is a regular farmer like many others across the UK, rearing dairy cows and planting crops, and just about getting by as the price of milk is kept incredibly low thanks to his main customers, the supermarkets. His son works beside him and is set to inherit the spread just as Derek did, while Derek’s wife, Linda, supplements their income by running holiday cottages.

articles.title: ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon
articles.summary: “Neagley” has been renewed for Season 2 at Amazon, Variety has learned. The “Reacher” spinoff series originally debuted on Prime Video on Sept. 16, the same day as the “Reacher” Season 4 finale.
body: Maria Sten reprises the role of Frances Neagley in the spinoff series, with Neagley having been Jack Reacher’s protege in the Army and now working as a private investigator. The logline for the debut season states, “When [Neagley] learns that a beloved friend from her past has been killed in a suspicious accident, she becomes hell-bent on justice.”

“Audiences around the world have embraced Frances Neagley as a force all her own,” said Peter Friedlander, head of global television for Amazon MGM Studios. “Maria Sten delivers a commanding, layered performance that drives every episode, and Nick Santora and Nicholas Wootton have built a world that is both thrilling and compelling. We are excited to continue this story and explore what’s next for Neagley with our partners at Paramount Television Studios.”
Along with Sten, the cast for Season 1 included Greyston Holt, Adeline Rudolph, Jasper Jones, Matthew Del Negro, and Damon Herriman. “Reacher” star Alan Ritchson appeared in a guest star role.

articles.title: ‘The Influencer Project’ Review: Found Footage Terror Takes a Tepid Danish Holiday
articles.summary: An opening text announcing “This film is influenced by real events” provides the first and last moment of inspiration in “The Influencer Project,” whether the joke is deliberate or not.
body: Copenhagen is to die for in Mike Nybroe’s decently crafted if over-familiar debut feature, in which Brit influencer Chiara King (playing herself) gets menaced by one very hostile, fictitious non-fan.

Yet as frightened as Chiara frequently is, and as concerned as the crew appear to be, somehow days keep going by without her ever thinking, “I gotta get the hell outta here.” When being hunted by a perp in a mask, what’s a person to do but dance at a nightclub where half the patrons are wearing glittery masks? Her follower count goes up whenever she appears scared. So even as danger rises, she visits “haunted houses” where something will inevitably get her running and screaming in dark corridors. Naturally, the climax takes place at a vast empty warehouse she and her remaining colleagues have been lured to. What could go wrong?

articles.title: Samantha Josephs’ Debut Horror Novel ‘Carrying’ to Receive Feature Adaptation From Tommy Dorfman’s Good Girl Productions (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Samantha Josephs’ upcoming debut horror novel “Carrying,” about a transgender woman living in secret who miraculously discovers she’s pregnant, is getting a feature adaptation from Tommy Dorfman’s Good Girl Productions.
body: Dorfman is set to direct and produce the project while Josephs will pen the screenplay.

Josephs is a New York native now living in Los Angeles. She graduated from USC’s Writing for the Screen and Television program and worked across podcasts, video games, apps and erotica before penning “Carrying.”

“From our very first meeting, it wasn’t just Tommy’s love for ‘Carrying’ that got me, but that she completely understood it,” Josephs said. “For a book that I know is extremely out there, it feels especially touching that she sees it and Martha so completely. As we’ve started working together, Tommy’s vision for my twisted tale has me absolutely giddy for everyone to experience. I know my baby is safe in Tommy’s capable hands.”

Actress and filmmaker Dorfman launched Good Girl Productions in 2025 with a focus on developing projects for film, television and theater. Other projects on the Good Girl slate include a feature adaptation of Torrey Peters’ bestseller “Detransition, Baby,” and a movie based on Allie Rowbottom’s thriller novel “Aestetica.”

articles.title: Nicolas Cage calls Marvel movies ‘a glorified WWE’ with over-50s in ‘ridiculous outfits’
articles.summary: Star of Spider-Noir told fan convention he ‘spoke with love’ at seeing gifted actors for ever gearing up for superhero fight scenes. Nicolas Cage, whose recent credits include the Sony Marvel series Spider-Noir, has criticised the Marvel Cinematic Universe, calling it an overfunded and embarrassing…
body: “I do say this with love,” said Cage at a fan convention in Texas. “When I see these 50-plus and otherwise intelligent and remarkably gifted thespians putting on these ridiculous outfits and getting ready for the fight – let’s face it, it’s all cutting to the fight – it’s hard for me not to be reminded that the MCU is becoming a well-funded and glorified WWE.”

Cage’s association with Marvel, the company run by comic book artist Stan Lee for many decades, includes not only Spider-Noir, which was cancelled after a single season, but also two movies in which he played the superhero Ghost Rider.

Cage, 62, told Variety his attraction to Spider-Noir was primarily aesthetic. “I wanted to try to create an essence of some of my favourite old world actors,” he said, “because I wanted to embody that style – Bogart, Cagney, Edward G Robinson – and designed my performance to fit within the black-and-white format.”

Other film stars and directors to express scepticism about Marvel movies include Martin Scorsese, who likened them to “theme parks”, and Francis Ford Coppola, who described the company as “despicable”.

articles.title: Kanye West's Russia shows officially cancelled after weeks of uncertainty
articles.summary: Chaos has surrounded the St Petersburg shows since the stadium said it had not agreed to host the rapper.
body: Two stadium gigs in Russia by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, have officially been cancelled.
West had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October.
But there was confusion in the lead-up to the shows, as the venue had said it wouldn't host him for what would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
In a post on messaging app Telegram, gig organisers Say Agency confirmed the concerts had been cancelled with "sincere regret".

articles.title: Tourette's campaigner Davidson asks to watch Scottish Baftas via video link after racial slur row
articles.summary: John Davidson, whose condition includes involuntary tics, shouted a racial slur during the Bafta Film Awards in February.
body: The movie I Swear, which tells the story of Davidson growing up with Tourette syndrome in Scotland in the 1980s, has been nominated for seven Scottish Baftas.
It scooped three prizes at the Bafta Film Awards in London in February.
But the event was overshadowed by Davidson, whose condition involves involuntary tics, shouting the N-word at presenters Michael B Jordan and Delroy Lindo.
The BBC later apologised for not editing out the slur from its BBC One broadcast, which was shown on a two-hour delay, and remained on BBC iPlayer until the following day.

articles.title: Aaron Sorkin Bets On Himself to Deliver a Worthy ‘Social Network’ Follow-Up. No Pressure
articles.summary: The screenwriter, who is also taking over the director's chair for 'Social Reckoning' while prepping a Broadway revival of 'A Few Good Men,' is keeping the film under wraps with few test screenings ahead of release.
body: Next week, Aaron Sorkin will see the theatrical release of The Social Reckoning, his long-awaited follow-up to The Social Network, as well as the start of the Broadway revival of A Few Good Men.

The leadup is stressful, not just because of the workload, the film premieres, the press frenzy, or, as Sorkin jokes to The Hollywood Reporter, “the potential for career immolation.” But also because Sorkin is returning to two topics that have been benchmarks in his career.

“I’m very proud of the film. I’m excited for people to see it, and I’m proud of the play. Probably, if I could choose, I wouldn’t have them happening at the same time. But it’s a pretty glamorous problem to have,” Sorkin says.

Sorkin is revisiting and refining A Few Good Men more than three decades after its Broadway premiere, which came after he penned the military court drama on cocktail napkins while working as a theater bartender. The play led to a feature film and helped launch the rest of his career. This production brings back Bradley Whitford (who made his debut in the original stage show), alongside Tom Blythe, and Krysta Rodriguez.
